questions.text: The Trans-Siberian Railway runs from Moscow to Vladivostok. How long is it, in kilometres?
questions.fact: The main line from Moscow to Vladivostok is 9,289 km (5,772 miles) long.

questions.text: Into how many prefectures is Japan divided?
questions.fact: Japan has 47: 43 ken, the two fu of Osaka and Kyoto, the do of Hokkaido and the to of Tokyo.

questions.text: How long is Switzerland's Gotthard Base Tunnel under the Alps, opened in 2016, in kilometres?
questions.fact: The twin-bore rail tunnel runs 57 km between Erstfeld and Bodio, up to about 2,000 m below the mountains.

questions.text: How many lakes larger than 500 square metres does Finland have, in thousands?
questions.fact: Finland counts 187,888 lakes of over 500 square metres, which rounds to 188 thousand.

questions.text: How long is the Grand Canyon, measured along the Colorado River, in kilometres?
questions.fact: It runs 277 river miles (446 km), from Lees Ferry to the Grand Wash Cliffs in Arizona.

questions.text: In what year was the Antarctic Treaty signed?
questions.fact: Twelve countries signed it in Washington, DC, on 1 December 1959, keeping Antarctica for peace and science.

questions.text: At what temperature does pure iron melt, in degrees Celsius?
questions.fact: Iron melts at 1,538 °C. It makes up about 5% of Earth's crust and most of its core.

questions.text: When Dmitri Mendeleev drew up his periodic table in 1869, how many elements did he arrange in it?
questions.fact: He ordered the 63 elements then known by atomic weight and left gaps for ones not yet found, such as gallium.

questions.text: How tall is the metal cylinder that defined the kilogram from 1889 to 2019, in millimetres?
questions.fact: Kept at the BIPM in France, it is about 39 mm tall and 39 mm wide, roughly golf-ball size: 90% platinum, 10% iridium.

questions.text: On average, how many days does a human red blood cell last in the body?
questions.fact: A red blood cell lasts about 120 days; then white blood cells called macrophages remove it.

questions.text: In what year did Watson and Crick publish the double-helix structure of DNA?
questions.fact: Their one-page paper appeared in the journal Nature on 25 April 1953.

questions.text: In what year did Isaac Newton publish his laws of motion in the 'Principia'?
questions.fact: The Principia came out in 1687; Edmond Halley paid for the printing himself.

questions.text: How many Earth days does Mars take to go once around the Sun?
questions.fact: A year on Mars lasts 687 Earth days, almost twice as long as ours.

questions.text: What is Earth's diameter at the Equator, in kilometres?
questions.fact: Earth is 12,756 km across at the Equator, a little more than from pole to pole.

questions.text: About how many Earths would fit side by side across the face of the Sun?
questions.fact: The Sun is about 109 times as wide as Earth; its surface area is about 12,000 times larger.

questions.text: How tall was the Saturn V rocket that took astronauts to the Moon, in metres?
questions.fact: Saturn V stood 110.6 m tall, about as high as a 36-storey building.

questions.text: Across the six Apollo Moon landings, how many kilograms of rock, soil and dust did astronauts bring back?
questions.fact: Twelve astronauts collected 382 kg (842 lb) of rocks, core samples, pebbles, sand and dust between 1969 and 1972.

questions.text: In what year was Pluto discovered?
questions.fact: Clyde Tombaugh found it on 18 February 1930 at Lowell Observatory in Arizona, aged 24.

questions.text: How many chromosomes are in each body cell of a dog?
questions.fact: Dogs have 78 chromosomes in 39 pairs; humans have 46.

questions.text: How many days does a fertile chicken egg take to hatch once incubation starts?
questions.fact: A fertile chicken egg hatches after about 21 days of incubation, kept warm and turned often.

questions.text: The first millipede known to have over 1,000 legs was described in 2021. How many legs did it have?
questions.fact: Eumillipes persephone, found 60 m underground in Western Australia, had 1,306; none known before had over 750.

questions.text: A hurricane reaches Category 5 at what sustained wind speed, in km/h?
questions.fact: On the Saffir-Simpson scale, Category 5 means sustained winds of 157 mph (252 km/h) or more.

questions.text: How many eyes does a box jellyfish have?
questions.fact: Box jellyfish have 24 eyes in four clusters of six, and some of them always point up at the sky.

questions.text: In what year was Yellowstone, widely seen as the world's first national park, set up?
questions.fact: President Ulysses S. Grant signed the law on 1 March 1872, setting the land aside as a "pleasuring-ground".

questions.text: How many signatures are on the US Declaration of Independence?
questions.fact: John Hancock signed first, and the other 55 delegates added their names over the following weeks.

questions.text: How many chests of tea were thrown into the harbour at the Boston Tea Party in 1773?
questions.fact: Protesters emptied 342 chests from three East India Company ships into Boston Harbor on 16 December 1773.

questions.text: How long is Hadrian's Wall, in modern miles?
questions.fact: The wall ran 73 miles (80 Roman miles) from Wallsend on the River Tyne to Bowness-on-Solway.

questions.text: For how many years did China's Ming dynasty rule?
questions.fact: The Ming ruled from 1368 to 1644; its founder, Zhu Yuanzhang, had once been a Buddhist monk.

questions.text: In what year did the Chinese admiral Zheng He set sail on the first of his seven great voyages?
questions.fact: His first fleet left in 1405 and sailed as far as Calicut in India; the seven voyages ran until 1433.

questions.text: In what year did Howard Carter find Tutankhamun's tomb?
questions.fact: Carter's team found the first step down to the tomb on 4 November 1922, in Egypt's Valley of the Kings.

questions.text: How many US patents did Thomas Edison receive?
questions.fact: Edison held 1,093 US patents, for things like the phonograph and electric light, and many more abroad.

questions.text: In 1963 Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space. How many orbits of the Earth did she make?
questions.fact: Her Vostok 6 flight lasted almost three days, about 71 hours, and went around the Earth 48 times.

questions.text: How old was Charles Darwin when he set sail on HMS Beagle?
questions.fact: Darwin sailed from Plymouth on 27 December 1831; the voyage lasted almost five years.

questions.text: How many nurses did Florence Nightingale take with her to the Crimean War in 1854?
questions.fact: Nightingale and 38 nurses reached the army hospital at Scutari, in Istanbul, on 4 November 1854.

questions.text: How many professional fights did the boxer Muhammad Ali have?
questions.fact: Ali won 56 (37 by knockout) and lost 5 of his 61 professional bouts.

questions.text: In what year did Amelia Earhart become the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic?
questions.fact: She flew a Lockheed Vega from Newfoundland to Northern Ireland, the second person after Lindbergh to do it solo.

questions.text: How wide is a football goal, between the posts, in centimetres?
questions.fact: A goal is 7.32 m (8 yards) wide and 2.44 m (8 feet) high, measured on the inside.

questions.text: What is the diameter of a golf hole, in millimetres?
questions.fact: The Rules of Golf set the hole at 108 mm (4.25 inches) across and at least 101.6 mm deep.

questions.text: How many teams played at the first FIFA World Cup, in 1930?
questions.fact: Uruguay hosted 13 teams in 1930: seven from South America, four from Europe and two from North America.

questions.text: How many feathers does a standard feathered badminton shuttlecock have?
questions.fact: The badminton rules call for 16 feathers fixed in a cork base, each 62 to 70 mm long.

questions.text: How many Olympic medals did the swimmer Michael Phelps win in his career?
questions.fact: Phelps won 28 Olympic medals, 23 of them gold.

questions.text: In what year was the first Wimbledon tennis championship held?
questions.fact: Spencer Gore won the first final in 1877, beating William Marshall; the event made a profit of £10.

questions.text: Erik Satie's one-page piano piece 'Vexations' has a note about playing its theme how many times in a row?
questions.fact: Satie's note speaks of playing the motif 840 times in succession, so a complete performance can last nearly a day.

questions.text: How many variations follow the aria in Bach's Goldberg Variations?
questions.fact: Bach's Goldberg Variations, published in 1741, are an aria followed by 30 variations.

questions.text: How many numbered piano sonatas did Beethoven write?
questions.fact: Beethoven's 32 numbered piano sonatas date from 1795 to 1822; three sonatas from his childhood are not counted.

questions.text: How long is Queen's single 'Bohemian Rhapsody', in seconds?
questions.fact: The single runs 5 minutes 55 seconds; it came out in the UK on 31 October 1975.

questions.text: In what year was Beethoven's Ninth Symphony first performed?
questions.fact: It was first played in Vienna on 7 May 1824, at the Kärntnertor Theatre.

questions.text: In what year were the Live Aid concerts held in London and Philadelphia?
questions.fact: Live Aid took place on one day, 13 July 1985, at Wembley Stadium and JFK Stadium.

questions.text: How many episodes of the sitcom 'Friends' were made?
questions.fact: Friends ran for 10 seasons, from 1994 to 2004, making 236 episodes.

questions.text: How many Oscars did the three 'Lord of the Rings' films win in total?
questions.fact: The films won 4, 2 and 11; 'The Return of the King' won every award it was nominated for.

questions.text: How many Oscars did the 1959 film 'Ben-Hur' win?
questions.fact: Ben-Hur won 11 of its 12 nominations, beating the record of 9 set by 'Gigi' the year before.

questions.text: In what year did the Lumière brothers hold the first paid public film show in Paris?
questions.fact: On 28 December 1895, at the Grand Café in Paris, they showed 10 short films.

questions.text: In what year was the first episode of 'Doctor Who' broadcast?
questions.fact: The first episode, 'An Unearthly Child', went out on BBC television on 23 November 1963.

questions.text: How many numbered chapters are in Herman Melville's 'Moby-Dick'?
questions.fact: Moby-Dick (1851) has 135 numbered chapters, followed by a short epilogue.

questions.text: How many plays are in Shakespeare's First Folio of 1623?
questions.fact: The First Folio's 36 plays include 18 never printed before, among them Macbeth and The Tempest.

questions.text: How many chapters are in 'The Tale of Genji', written in Japan around 1010?
questions.fact: Murasaki Shikibu's Tale of Genji, from about 1010, runs to 54 chapters.

questions.text: How many lines long is the Old English poem 'Beowulf'?
questions.fact: Beowulf survives in a single manuscript from around 1000, which was damaged by fire in 1731.

questions.text: How many lines are in the standard Greek text of Homer's 'Iliad'?
questions.fact: The Iliad's 15,693 lines are split into 24 books.

questions.text: In what year was the first part of 'Don Quixote' published?
questions.fact: Part One of Cervantes's novel came out in Madrid in 1605; Part Two followed in 1615.

questions.text: How tall is the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, to its tip, in metres?
questions.fact: The Burj Khalifa opened on 4 January 2010; its height of 828 m was confirmed by the CTBUH.

questions.text: How many columns stand around the outside of the Parthenon in Athens?
questions.fact: There are 8 columns at each end and 17 along each side, 46 in all. It was built in 447-432 BC.

questions.text: How wide is Leonardo da Vinci's mural 'The Last Supper', in centimetres?
questions.fact: The mural is 460 × 880 cm, painted on a dry wall in Milan rather than as a true fresco.

questions.text: How tall is the Empire State Building to its roof, not counting the mast, in feet?
questions.fact: The 102-storey building is 1,250 ft to the roof; it opened in New York in 1931.

questions.text: How tall is the Elizabeth Tower, home of Big Ben, in metres?
questions.fact: The tower is 96 m tall, with 334 steps up to the belfry; it was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012.

questions.text: In what year did building work start on the Sagrada Família in Barcelona?
questions.fact: The first stone was laid on 19 March 1882; Antoni Gaudí took charge of the project a year later.

questions.text: Under EU rules, butter may contain at most what percentage of water?
questions.fact: EU butter must be at least 80% (but under 90%) milk fat, with at most 16% water.

questions.text: A standard Bordeaux barrique wine barrel holds how many litres?
questions.fact: A Bordeaux barrique holds 225 litres, about 300 bottles; a Burgundy barrel holds 228.

questions.text: A Nebuchadnezzar wine bottle holds as much as how many standard 75 cl bottles?
questions.fact: A Nebuchadnezzar holds 15 litres, the same as 20 standard 75 cl bottles.

questions.text: Vintage Champagne must age for at least how many months before it can be sold?
questions.fact: Vintage Champagne must age at least three years; non-vintage needs at least 15 months.

questions.text: Under the EU's 2010 rules for 'Pizza Napoletana', what is the largest allowed diameter, in centimetres?
questions.fact: The rules allow up to 35 cm across, with a centre about 0.4 cm thick and a raised rim of 1 to 2 cm.

questions.text: In what year did Momofuku Ando launch the first instant noodles?
questions.fact: Ando brought out Chicken Ramen in Japan in 1958, when he was 48.

questions.text: How many different words did Dr. Seuss use to write 'The Cat in the Hat' (1957)?
questions.fact: Challenged to write a fun first reader from a short list of words for new readers, Dr. Seuss used just 236 different words.

questions.text: The Welsh village usually shortened to Llanfair PG has a full name of how many characters?
questions.fact: The full name has 58 characters but only 51 Welsh letters, as 'll' and 'ch' each count as one letter.

questions.text: According to Guinness World Records, how many letters does the Khmer alphabet of Cambodia have?
questions.fact: Guinness lists Khmer, with 74 letters (some no longer used), as the longest alphabet.

questions.text: How many characters fit in one standard text message (SMS) using the basic alphabet?
questions.fact: An SMS carries 140 bytes; in the basic 7-bit alphabet that is 160 characters, or 70 with Unicode.

questions.text: In what year was the first modern crossword published?
questions.fact: Arthur Wynne's 'word-cross' puzzle appeared in the New York World on 21 December 1913.

questions.text: In what year did Samuel Johnson publish his 'Dictionary of the English Language'?
questions.fact: Johnson's dictionary came out in two large volumes on 15 April 1755.

questions.text: How many different legal first moves does White have in chess?
questions.fact: White's 20 possible first moves are 16 pawn moves and 4 knight moves.

questions.text: How many cards are in a standard tarot deck?
questions.fact: A tarot deck has 22 major arcana and 56 minor arcana cards, in four suits of 14.

questions.text: What is the fewest starting clues a standard Sudoku can have and still have only one solution?
questions.fact: A 2012 computer search proved that no 16-clue Sudoku has a unique solution, so 17 is the minimum.

questions.text: How long is a sheet of A4 paper, in millimetres?
questions.fact: A4 is 210 × 297 mm; each A size is half the one before, starting from A0 at 1 square metre.

questions.text: In how many ways can six 2×4 LEGO bricks of one colour be put together, in millions?
questions.fact: Mathematician Søren Eilers counted 915,103,765 ways; LEGO's old 1974 figure was 102,981,500.

questions.text: In what year did Fibonacci publish 'Liber Abaci', which helped bring Hindu-Arabic numerals to Europe?
questions.fact: Liber Abaci (1202) helped spread Hindu-Arabic numerals in Europe and set the rabbit problem behind the Fibonacci numbers.

questions.text: How long is the main span of San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge, between its towers, in metres?
questions.fact: The 1,280 m (4,200 ft) main span was the longest in the world from 1937 until 1964.

questions.text: How many transistors were on the Intel 4004 of 1971, the first commercial microprocessor?
questions.fact: Launched on 15 November 1971, the Intel 4004 packed about 2,300 transistors onto one chip.

questions.text: How many kilobytes of memory did the first Apple Macintosh have in 1984?
questions.fact: The Macintosh 128K had an 8 MHz 68000 processor and a 9-inch black-and-white screen.

questions.text: How many lines of text are on most pages of the Gutenberg Bible?
questions.fact: Most pages have 42 lines, so it is also called the 42-line Bible; the first pages had 40 or 41.

questions.text: In what year was a product barcode first scanned at a shop checkout?
questions.fact: A pack of Wrigley's gum was scanned on 26 June 1974 at a supermarket in Troy, Ohio.
